issue.title: [Bug] 原生 Responses 中继缺少明文协作标记，Codex V2 子任务丢失（v0.1.1311）
issue.body:
## 问题范围

这是 #141 和 #613 的原生 Responses 中继分支后续问题，不是认为已有翻译路径修复未发布。

在 Magpie `v0.1.1311` 中，供应商启用 Responses 后，明文 `collaboration.spawn_agent` 回复没有 `encrypted_function_args: []`。使用真实 Codex V2 客户端时，任务因此进入子代理的 `encrypted_content`，子代理未执行任务，只返回“请告诉我需要处理的任务”。

## 环境

- macOS，Magpie `0.1.1311`，构建提交 `82fb0702fc43fd8a12f4d69e279676f47baf175b`。
- Codex Desktop 包内二进制 `0.163.0-alpha.10.2`。
- 现有自定义供应商别名 `ucloud/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`，对应 UCloud 提供的 DeepSeek 模型，不是 DeepSeek 官方 API 的认证测试。
- 供应商声明 Responses 可用，模型目录中的 `native_endpoints` 包含 `/v1/responses`。
- 只通过本次 CLI 进程启用 V2，没有修改全局配置。该测试是桌面包内后端的 CLI 执行，不是桌面 UI V2 验收。

## 实际 V2 复现

对当前已接入本机 Magpie 的配置，使用同一个内置二进制执行以下参数。

```sh
"$CODEX_BIN" exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only \
  --enable multi_agent --enable multi_agent_v2 \
  -c 'model_provider="magpie"' -c 'web_search="disabled"' \
  -c 'model_reasoning_effort="high"' \
  --model ucloud/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --json \
  'Run printf for a parent control token. Spawn exactly one native child without inherited context or model override. Tell it to execute printf for DSV2_T9P4_CHILD_TOOL_OK, then reply exactly DSV2_T9P4_CHILD_RECEIVED. Wait for actual completion. Do not create a replacement if it fails.'
```

实测时给子代理的完整 message 如下。

```text
Do not read or write any files or access network. Execute printf 'DSV2_T9P4_CHILD_TOOL_OK\n' using exec_command. Then reply exactly DSV2_T9P4_CHILD_RECEIVED.
```

从精确的父子 rollout 读回，验证得到以下结果。

1. 父级与子级的 `turn_context.multi_agent_version` 都是 `v2`，模型均为上述别名。
2. 父级实际执行了控制命令，stdout 与预设 token 一致。
3. 父级实际调用 `collaboration.spawn_agent`，参数为 `fork_turns: "none"` 和上面的明文 message。返回的 `function_call` 完全没有 `encrypted_function_args` 字段，不是空数组。
4. 子级收到 `agent_message`，其中有 NEW_TASK 的 `input_text` 前缀，但完整可读的原始 message 被放在另一个 `encrypted_content` 项中。该字符串与父级 message 完全相同，并不是真正的密文。
5. 子级没有任何 `exec_command` 调用，也没有返回目标 nonce。最终回复是“已就绪。请告诉我需要处理的任务；我会按任务类型选择匹配技能，并先确认范围再执行。”
6. CLI 最终退出 0，但子任务目标失败。没有根据退出码或模型自述判定通过。

在对应公开 Codex 源码的 [`ToolCall::direct_source`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0-alpha.10/codex-rs/core/src/tools/router.rs#L56) 中，这三个 `collaboration` message 工具只有在 `encrypted_function_args` 明确存在且为空时才选择 `DirectPlaintextMessage`，与本轮的误分类行为一致。

CLI 同时提示这个模型别名未命中其模型目录并使用 fallback metadata。这里保留该限制，实际 V2 模式不是从请求参数推断，而是由父子原始 turn context 确认。

## 同分支的独立网关对照

不执行任何工具，仅向本机 `/v1/responses` 发送以下合法数组形式的任务。

```json
{
  "model": "ucloud/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017",
  "max_output_tokens": 256,
  "stream": false,
  "input": [{
    "type": "agent_message",
    "author": "/root",
    "recipient": "/root/worker",
    "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": "Reply with exactly DSAFTER_N6T2_ARRAY. Do not use tools."}]
  }]
}
```

两次实际请求都得到上游 `400 InvalidParameter`，具体错误为 `unknown type: agent_message`。仅把该 input 转为 `type: message, role: user` 并保留相同正文，经同一个网关和同一个模型得到 200，准确返回 `DSAFTER_N6T2_ARRAY`。

另一个真实探针提供带 `encrypted: true` 参数的 `collaboration.spawn_agent`，上游返回 200。JSON 回复，以及 SSE 的 `response.output_item.added`、`response.output_item.done`、`response.completed.response.output`，都保留了 namespace 和明文参数，但都缺少空的加密参数列表。200 并不能证明 V2 后续传递正确。

## 与已有修复的区别

- #141 的 `parseResponses` 和 `callTo` 修复已在 `v0.1.267` 发布，后续 open 状态用于跟踪 V1 选项。这两个修复仍存在。
- #613 的加密 schema 与流式参数修复也已发布。
- 在 `v0.1.1311` 源码的 `Server.attempt` / `passthrough` 分支上，原生 Responses 中继未统一经过上述解析和命名空间回复编码。本轮在该发布提交的真实 handler 上，使用 loopback 假上游再次确认了同样的请求和回复行为。
- `responses.go` 和 `Server.attempt` 的相关逻辑与升级前固定源码一致，所以这里报告分支覆盖缺口，不声称升级引入了新回归。
- 同配置的桌面会话 V1 已实际完成父级命令、子代理命令、追加任务和结果回传。V1 通过不代表这个 V2 分支通过。

## 期望与边界

请考虑让不封装协作密文的第三方 Responses 路径也获得明文协作适配，或明确提供对应的供应商能力选择，使这些调用不会被客户端当成密文，且上游不认识的明文 `agent_message` 能转换为实际任务正文。

需要保留真正支持密文的 OpenAI 原生路径。这里不要求解密真实 OpenAI 密文，不要求给任意同名顶层普通函数补协作 namespace，也不把 compact text、单对象 content 或缺少必要 `call_id` 的宽容扩展当成标准 Codex 缺陷。

comments.body:
## Summary

The branch of #141/#613 that no fix reached is the relay. On a vendor serving the Responses API natively, Codex's request is relayed as it came (`Server.passthrough`, internal/gateway/gateway.go:4179) — and the vendor's reply went back as it came too. A vendor that answers `collaboration.spawn_agent` with its plain-text arguments but no `encrypted_function_args` field (exactly what the issue's probe recorded: namespace kept, arguments kept, no list) handed Codex a call Codex cannot read as a plain-text task: `ToolCall::direct_source` (codex-rs tools/router.rs, rust-v0.163.0) picks `DirectPlaintextMessage` only when `encrypted_function_args` is present and empty. So Codex took the task for sealed, wrapped the readable message in an `encrypted_content` of its own under the NEW_TASK header, and the subagent — handed ciphertext it cannot open, which is really plain text — asked what the task was and did nothing. That is the issue's item 3-5.

The translated path has said "not sealed" since #613: `callTo` gives every namespaced call `encrypted_function_args: []` (internal/gateway/responses.go:1711, "Nothing magpie serves seals arguments"). The Grok and Zed relays have had it through `nsTidy` since #404 (internal/gateway/grok_namespace.go). The one place neither reached is the relay to any other vendor: `namespacedIn` was read only for Grok and Zed (internal/gateway/gateway.go:4385 at base), so no relayed reply ever carried the word.

## Cause

The relay's response side passes a vendor's reply through a row of small tidies, and the only one that knows Codex's namespaces was gated to two plugins. A vendor asked as Codex sends it keeps the namespace in its tools and says it back on the call; what is missing from its reply is not the name, it is the empty list — the one bit Codex reads to tell a plain-text task from a sealed one. Nothing magpie serves seals arguments on this path either: the marks in spawn_agent's schema go upstream only as schema, and the issue's probe confirms the vendor answers 200 with plain arguments and no list.

## Fix

The namespaced tools a Responses request offers are now read on every relay, not only Grok's and Zed's (internal/gateway/gateway.go, the `named` computation in `passthrough`), and `nsTidy.call` (internal/gateway/grok_namespace.go) now also handles a call whose namespace the upstream named itself: when (namespace, name) matches a tool the request offered and the call carries no `encrypted_function_args`, the empty list is added — the same shape `callTo` gives the translated path. A call that does carry a seal — OpenAI's own, or any upstream that answers the mark — goes back with that seal untouched, and a call to a tool outside every namespace says nothing about seals either way (both locked by `TestNativeRelayLeavesOtherCallsBe`). The loop closes on the way back: the field Codex replays of it in a later turn's history is still what `forVendor` leaves out of what a non-OpenAI vendor is asked (`openaiOnly`, internal/gateway/codex_backend.go:2422), so the vendor never sees it.

## Verification

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `TestNativeRelayNamespacedCallSaysUnsealed` (stub vendor, stream and whole; asserts the relay, not a translation, and the empty list on every function_call Codex reads) | red on base, green with the fix |
| ablation: fix removed (`git checkout` of the two source files) | red, same assertion, `native_relay_collab_test.go:122`; fix restored, green |
| mutation: the list filled (`[]any{""}`) | red — a non-empty list is not "unsealed"; restored, green |
| `TestNativeRelayLeavesOtherCallsBe` (sealed call, plain call) | green: the seal survives, the plain call stays bare |
| `go test ./internal/gateway -count=1` (full package) | ok 322.6s |
| the new tests + the #404/#613 namespace tests, `-race` | ok |
| `gofmt -l`, `go vet ./internal/gateway` | clean |
| `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -tags nogui` darwin/arm64, linux/amd64, windows/amd64 | ok |

## Not verified

Not tried against the reporter's vendor or a real Codex Desktop; the stub's reply is the shape their probe recorded. The issue's second wish — a plaintext `agent_message` input item an upstream doesn't know turned into task text (their hand-built probe's 400 `unknown type: agent_message`) — is not addressed here: the real V2 rollout failed at the classification, before any `agent_message` went upstream, and reshaping every relayed conversation that carries one is a separate decision (the Grok relay does it in `grokAgentMessage`; a native relay doing it for every vendor is a bigger change than this branch needs).

---

**Source**: reported in #3183 (john-zeng-233, with V2 rollout records).

**Red without the fix** (base `f5b01574`):

```
--- FAIL: TestNativeRelayNamespacedCallSaysUnsealed (0.11s)
    native_relay_collab_test.go:122: stream true: Codex was given map[arguments: call_id:c9 id:fc_1 name:spawn_agent namespace:collaboration type:function_call]
FAIL
FAIL	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gateway	1.009s
```

(the call Codex was given carries no `encrypted_function_args` — the issue's item 3.)

**Siblings**: the field has three handling points, all now saying the same thing. The translated path adds the empty list in `callTo` (internal/gateway/responses.go:1711, #613); the request side strips what Codex replays of it before a non-OpenAI vendor is asked (`forVendor`/`openaiOnly`, internal/gateway/codex_backend.go:2422); the relay now adds it in `nsTidy.call` for a call named with its namespace (and, as since #404, renames a flat `collaboration__spawn_agent` back for the plugins that were offered it flat). No other spot in the tree reads or writes the field. The V1 spawn path, the spawn_agent models list and the session viewers do not touch it.

**When an upstream seals for real**: a reply whose namespaced call carries `encrypted_function_args` — OpenAI's own relays, or a vendor that honours the schema mark — passes with its seal exactly as it came; the fix adds nothing beside an absent list, and Codex's own handling of a seal it cannot open is unchanged.

Branch with the commit: [hunt57-e-native-relay-collab](https://github.com/ggbdpq/magpie/tree/hunt57-e-native-relay-collab) (head `9fff5bab`).

**Patch**: 3 files changed, 189 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-). SHA-256 first 16: `1b3f7c114dcf2c15`.

```patch
for darwin/arm64, linux/amd64 and windows/amd64. Not tried against the
reporter's vendor; the stub's reply is the shape their probe recorded

+// asked what the task was. Codex picks DirectPlaintextMessage only when
+// the list is there and empty, as the translated path's callTo gives it.
+func TestNativeRelayNamespacedCallSaysUnsealed(t *testing.T) {
+	fresh(t)
+	var mu sync.Mutex
+	var sent []map[string]any
+	call := `{"type":"function_call","id":"fc_1","call_id":"c9","name":"spawn_agent","namespace":"collaboration","arguments":"{\"message\":\"go\"}","status":"completed"}`
+	up := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+		b, _ := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
+		var q map[string]any
+		json.Unmarshal(b, &q)
+		mu.Lock()
+		sent = append(sent, q)
+		mu.Unlock()
+		done := `{"id":"r1","object":"response","status":"completed","output":[` + call + `],"usage":{"input_tokens":5,"output_tokens":3}}`
+		if q["stream"] != true {
+			w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
+			io.WriteString(w, done)
+			return
+		}
+		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
+		io.WriteString(w, sse(
+			`event: response.created`+"\n"+`data: {"type":"response.created","response":{"id":"r1","object":"response","status":"in_progress","output":[]}}`,
+			`event: response.output_item.added`+"\n"+`data: {"type":"response.output_item.added","output_index":0,"item":{"type":"function_call","id":"fc_1","call_id":"c9","name":"spawn_agent","namespace":"collaboration","arguments":""}}`,
+			`event: response.output_item.done`+"\n"+`data: {"type":"response.output_item.done","output_index":0,"item":`+call+`}`,
+			`event: response.completed`+"\n"+`data: {"type":"response.completed","response":`+done+`}`))
+	}))
+	defer up.Close()
+	if err := provider.Save(provider.Provider{ID: "ucloud", Name: "UCloud", Key: "k", Models: []string{"m"}, Responses: up.URL + "/v1"}); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	s := New()
+	for _, stream := range []bool{true, false} {
+		mu.Lock()
+		sent = nil
+		mu.Unlock()
+		body := `{"model":"ucloud/m","stream":` + map[bool]string{true: "true", false: "false"}[stream] + `,` + codexCollabTools + `,"input":[{"type":"message","role":"user","content":"go"}]}`
+		rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
+		s.Handler().ServeHTTP(rec, httptest.NewRequest("POST", "/v1/responses", strings.NewReader(body)))
+		if rec.Code != 200 {
+			t.Fatalf("stream %v: %d %s", stream, rec.Code, rec.Body)
+		}
+		// relayed, not translated: the namespace went up as Codex sent it
+		mu.Lock()
+		if len(sent) != 1 {
+			t.Fatalf("stream %v: the vendor was asked %d times", stream, len(sent))
+		}
+		q := sent[0]
+		mu.Unlock()
+		tools, _ := q["tools"].([]any)
+		if len(tools) != 2 {
+			t.Fatalf("stream %v: the vendor was offered %v", stream, q["tools"])
+		}
+		if tm, _ := tools[1].(map[string]any); tm["type"] != "namespace" || tm["name"] != "collaboration" {
+			t.Fatalf("stream %v: the request was translated, its tools went as %v", stream, q["tools"])
+		}
+
+		// every function_call Codex reads says its arguments are plain text
+		var items []map[string]any
+		if stream {
+			for _, line := range strings.Split(rec.Body.String(), "\n") {
+				data, ok := strings.CutPrefix(line, "data: ")
+				if !ok {
+					continue
+				}
+				var ev struct {
+					Item     map[string]any `json:"item"`
+					Response struct {
+						Output []map[string]any `json:"output"`
+					} `json:"response"`
+				}
+				if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(data), &ev); err != nil {
+					t.Fatalf("%v: %s", err, data)
+				}
+				if ev.Item != nil {
+					items = append(items, ev.Item)
+				}
+				items = append(items, ev.Response.Output...)
+			}
+		} else {
+			var res struct {
+				Output []map[string]any `json:"output"`
+			}
+			if err := json.Unmarshal(rec.Body.Bytes(), &res); err != nil {
+				t.Fatalf("%v: %s", err, rec.Body)
+			}
+			items = res.Output
+		}
+		if len(items) == 0 || stream && len(items) != 3 {
+			t.Fatalf("stream %v: %s", stream, rec.Body)
+		}
+		for _, it := range items {
+			sealed, ok := it["encrypted_function_args"].([]any)

+			}
+		}
+	}
+}

+// answered a namespaced call with its arguments sealed hands that seal on
+// untouched, and a call to a tool outside every namespace says nothing

+func TestNativeRelayLeavesOtherCallsBe(t *testing.T) {
+	fresh(t)
+	sealed := `{"type":"function_call","id":"fc_1","call_id":"c9","name":"spawn_agent","namespace":"collaboration","arguments":"","encrypted_function_args":[{"content":"gAAAAAsealed"}],"status":"completed"}`

+		io.ReadAll(r.Body)

+		io.WriteString(w, `{"id":"r1","object":"response","status":"completed","output":[`+sealed+`,`+plain+`],"usage":{"input_tokens":5,"output_tokens":3}}`)
+	}))
+	defer up.Close()
+	if err := provider.Save(provider.Provider{ID: "ucloud", Name: "UCloud", Key: "k", Models: []string{"m"}, Responses: up.URL + "/v1"}); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	s := New()
+	body := `{"model":"ucloud/m","stream":false,` + codexCollabTools + `,"input":[{"type":"message","role":"user","content":"go"}]}`
+	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
+	s.Handler().ServeHTTP(rec, httptest.NewRequest("POST", "/v1/responses", strings.NewReader(body)))
+	if rec.Code != 200 {
+		t.Fatalf("%d %s", rec.Code, rec.Body)

+	var res struct {
+		Output []map[string]any `json:"output"`
+	}
+	if err := json.Unmarshal(rec.Body.Bytes(), &res); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)

+	if len(res.Output) != 2 {
+		t.Fatalf("%s", rec.Body.String())
+	}
+	if got, ok := res.Output[0]["encrypted_function_args"].([]any); !ok || len(got) != 1 {
+		t.Fatalf("the seal was lost: %v", res.Output[0])
+	}
+	if _, ok := res.Output[1]["encrypted_function_args"]; ok {
+		t.Fatalf("a plain call was given a seal: %v", res.Output[1])
+	}
+}
```

怀疑补充空数组的逻辑将 CPA 转发的封装任务错误标记成明文。能否区分普通明文 Responses 服务与转发原生封装任务的中继？

目前已做版本回退验证，尚未做单独撤销该提交的验证，也未抓取 CPA → Magpie 的原始响应确认字段最初在哪一层缺失。

我这边也遇到了和 @oevery 类似的情况，补充一组对照结果。

环境是 macOS，Magpie 0.1.3058，Codex 桌面内置后端 0.166.0-alpha.6，通过自定义 Responses 中转使用 gpt-6.1-sol。

用相同的业务输入分别直连上游和经过 Magpie，请求没有压缩项，也不执行模型生成的工具调用：

- 直连上游：`spawn_agent.message` 是 `gAAAA…` 格式的载荷，`encrypted_function_args` 字段缺失。
- 经过 Magpie：载荷仍是同类格式，但多了 `encrypted_function_args: []`。

实际 V2 子会话中也能看到，任务载荷被作为普通 `input_text` 交付，子代理回复无法读取任务。

对照 0.1.3058 的 `nsTidy.call`，这里会把缺失字段补成空数组。但对这种保留原生密封任务的中转，字段缺失似乎不能直接当作“参数是明文”。能否考虑让这类中转显式选择保留 Codex 原生加密标记的模式？仅凭 `gAAAA` 前缀判断也未必可靠。

补充一组与上面两条中转回归反馈一致的实测：**真实密文可以正常解密；只修正加密标记就恢复父子代理双向通信，恢复原网关行为后立即再次失败。** 另发现现有 fork 补丁没有覆盖本次 `arguments` 内嵌 JSON `message` 的数据形态。

**环境**

- Windows，Codex Desktop 内置后端 `0.167.0-alpha.3.2`，原生 `collaboration` / multi-agent V2。
- 实际采样和对照时 Magpie 为 `0.1.3335`，由应用启动日志确认。
- 自定义 API-key Responses 提供商，主、子代理均经同一提供商使用 `gpt-6-astra`；下文匿名记为 `relay/gpt-6-astra`。
- 2026-11-08，北京时间；测试发生在普通聊天中，不限于审查模式。

**1. 在 Magpie 改写前观察真实上游响应**

临时将该提供商的 Responses 地址指向仅监听 loopback 的转发器，再转发到原上游，沿用原网络代理和实际 Codex 请求。请求正文保持不变，没有伪造官方客户端标头。只保存必要协议元数据、长度和哈希，不记录凭据、完整对话或原始密文。

23:08 的同一次 `collaboration.followup_task`：

| 位置 | `encrypted_function_args` | 任务正文 / 接收方式 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 上游 → Magpie，改写前 | 字段缺失 | `arguments` 为 JSON 字符串，其中 `message` 是密文 |
| Codex 保存的工具调用 | `[]` | `message` 与上游完全相同 |
| 子代理收到的消息 | 已走明文投递 | `input_text` 含同一密文，子代理报告不可读 |

上游 SSE 的 `response.output_item.added`、`response.output_item.done`、`response.completed` 都缺少该字段，不是结束事件补回了标记。请求中的 `message.encrypted: true` 仍存在。完成事件、Codex 工具参数和接收端正文的 SHA-256 一致。

**2. 只改标记的真实对照实验**

23:32–23:33，继续使用同一个已有子代理。临时转发器只对这两个测试聊天的 `followup_task` / `send_message` 做诊断性修改：

- 对缺字段且 `arguments` 为空的初始 `output_item.added` 补 `encrypted_function_args: null`，避免 Magpie 补成空数组。
- 完成事件确认本次测试的 `message` 是密文形态后，给缺字段的调用补 `["message"]`；已有标记不覆盖。
- 不修改请求正文或消息密文；每次执行均核对上游、Codex 参数和接收端的正文哈希一致。这是受控诊断规则，不是建议直接上线的通用密文识别方案。

| 条件 | 观察到的实际结果 |
| --- | --- |
| 原网关行为 | 密文 + `[]` → `input_text`，消息不可读 |
| 仅修正标记 | Codex 保存 `["message"]`，接收端为 `encrypted_content`；追加任务、父到子的普通消息、子到父的普通消息均可读 |
| 23:34 恢复原网关 | 再次为 `[]` + `input_text`，同一子代理立即报告新任务不可读 |

第一次追加任务要求子代理通过 `send_message` 回传一个新口令，父代理能读懂，子代理最终答复也准确回传。第二次把另一个新口令仅放在父到子的普通消息里，再发不包含口令的追加任务要求读取它，子代理再次准确回传。没有用共享文件传任务或结果。共核对四次实际执行的修正调用，一次客户端取消后重试的生成尝试未算作成功执行。

转发器先通过 18 项隔离检查，涵盖透传/断流、JSON/SSE、会话范围、显式标记保留、当前实体网关保留修正标记，以及正常退出/超时/进程终止后的恢复。测试结束已恢复原 Responses 地址，提供商其他字段未变；没有替换正式网关二进制，也没有留下永久转发方案。

这组对照说明：本次密文的生成和解密链路可用，Magpie 的标记改写足以造成失败。历史上为何同一配置曾返回明文、后来返回密文仍未确定；不据此将变化归因于某次版本升级。本轮复用已有子代理，没有重新测试 `spawn_agent` 初始任务。

**3. `c20d3e202` 的覆盖缺口：密文在 JSON 的 `message` 里**

感谢提供 [fork 修复 c20d3e202](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/c20d3e202788edac7021d506a81207d04a315e08)。检查该提交发现，守卫对整个 `it["arguments"]` 字符串匹配：

```go
if args, _ := it["arguments"].(string); nativeSealedAgentPayload.MatchString(args) {
    return false
}
```

对应正则是 `^gAAAAA[A-Za-z0-9_-]+={0,2}$`，新增测试也把整个 `arguments` 直接设为 token。但本次真实结构是下面这样（值已替换，不是真实密文）：

```json
{
  "type": "function_call",
  "namespace": "collaboration",
  "name": "followup_task",
  "arguments": "{\"target\":\"/root/probe\",\"message\":\"gAAAAA...\"}"
}
```

对实际参数做只读核对：整个 `arguments` 不匹配该正则，解析后的 `message` 匹配。因此这个守卫不会保护本次形态；测试还需要覆盖嵌套字段，以及初始参数为空、参数完成、output-item 完成和整次 response 完成的 SSE 阶段。本次没有安装或运行该 fork，这一结论来自代码和实际报文结构核对。

查询时的主仓 `main` 及最新发布 [v0.1.3336 的 `nsTidy.call`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.3336/internal/gateway/grok_namespace.go#L186-L222) 仍在 namespace 匹配且缺字段时无条件补 `[]`。

希望修复能在保留真正明文提供商兼容行为的同时，保留支持原生密封消息的第三方 Responses 中转的加密语义，并覆盖上述 JSON 内 `message` 及流式阶段。这里补充的是实际边界采样和可逆干预证据，不主张只靠密文前缀就能完整判定所有提供商协议。

@WilliamK7 谢谢这组边界采样及 A/B/A 实测。你指出的覆盖缺口成立：`c20d3e202` 只匹配整个 arguments；JSON 对象中的 `message` 不受它保护，初始空 arguments 也没有分类依据。此前我们把这个守卫描述成完整修复，范围说大了。

Real-traffic feedback on v0.1.3526 (running 0.1.3690): the fix works, and it exposed a separate, still-present bug in the sealed gate. Details below, everything anonymized (a Sub2API relay behind a custom provider entry, one fresh lead conversation, two subagents spawned in it, `fork_turns="none"`).

## The fix is confirmed working

- `spawn_agent`'s `message` was a `gAAAAA…` token, and the relayed reply now carries `encrypted_function_args: ["message"]`; plaintext-arg calls (`wait_agent`, `list_agents`) still get `[]`. Exactly the intended split.
- Subagent #2 (`vcp-codex/gpt-6-astra`, a different model from the lead's `vcp-codex/gpt-6.1-sol`, same relay) completed end-to-end: the sealed task was opened upstream, both directions readable, plaintext FINAL_ANSWER. So yes — on this version lead and subagent read each other again, including cross-model within one relay.

## Still present: the first spawn of a fresh conversation can be refused with lead="" 

Subagent #1 (same slug as the lead: `vcp-codex/gpt-6.1-sol`) was turned away locally — HTTP 400 in 12 ms, never sent upstream — with the third `sealedTaskError` branch: "…magpie has no record of it answering the lead in the last 30 days", while the lead was at that moment being answered by that exact provider+model.

Timeline (ms-precision, relative):

| t | event |
|---|---|
| +12.5s | lead conversation's first completed turn written to usage: provider `vcp-codex`, kind null, status 200 — passes every `loggedAnswers` filter |
| **+21.0s** | subagent #1's first request → sealed gate: `leadProvider` finds no stick, `loggedAnswerers(parent, conv)` returns nothing → `lead=""` → 400 |
| +21.6s | the lead's spawning turn (10.9 s long) completes and is written — the check ran **0.6 s before** this row existed |
| +33s | subagent #2's first request → both lookups now hit → 200, full success |

So the miss is spawn-order, not model identity: Codex spawns the subagent mid-stream, so the subagent's first request structurally precedes the spawning turn's completion, and in a fresh conversation the only earlier row (+12.5s, which qualifies under every filter in `loggedAnswers`) still wasn't visible to either lookup at +21.0s — no affinity stick for the conversation yet, and/or the `readLogSnapshot` settle-stamp window (#4368) had not re-read the log. `sealed_lead_record_test.go` covers the 30-day fallback but not this window.

Question: is the gate meant to rely on the spawning turn being recorded first? For a fresh conversation's first spawn that can never hold. If so, maybe the in-flight answerer (the gateway knows it is serving the lead's turn right then) or the conversation's own earlier completed turns could count.

Context: the relay itself drops `encrypted_function_args` on its HTTP path (Wei-Shaw/sub2api#8582), which is why magpie's `["message"]` rewrite is load-bearing here — with it, the end-to-end sealed flow through the relay works.

Read the gate at today's main (`f6c882ad7`, which carries the 30-day stick from `45dfdd998`). Your timeline is real in the code, and the direct answer to your question is: **the gate is not meant to rely on the spawning turn being recorded first** — the log fallback exists precisely because affinity can miss (#1367) — but that safety net has two gaps a fresh conversation's first spawn can fall through.

**The order you describe is structural.** The gate reads `leadProvider(scope, parent)` — the affinity stick — then, if the reader set doesn't take it, falls back to `loggedAnswerers(parent, conv)` (gateway.go, the `sealedTask` block). A stick is written only when an answer completes (`answered`, affinity.go, called with the call's usage once the turn is done), never while the request is out. Codex spawns the subagent mid-stream of the lead's turn, so the subagent's first request structurally precedes the stick the spawning turn will write. Subagent #2 at +33 s found both lookups; subagent #1 at +21.0 s, 0.6 s before the spawning turn's row, had neither.

**Why the +12.5 s row was invisible is the open half.** Two candidates, and your data doesn't yet tell them apart:

1. **The fallback reads the shared snapshot, not the file.** `loggedAnswers` → `usage.VisitSessions` → `readLogSnapshot()`. While appends keep the file inside the settle stamp (`logStampSettle` = 1 s), a reader keeps the previous snapshot without re-hashing — #4368's own comment: "Still in the stamp's tick: hashing the log again proves nothing a read a moment earlier wouldn't have". Under traffic appending more often than once a second, the snapshot — and everything this fallback sees — lags until a quiet second. Your +12.5 s row could be in the file but not yet in the index the gate reads.
2. **Or the row never matches.** `loggedAnswers` matches Session/NativeSession against the ids the gate passes; if the lead's first turn recorded a different session id than the `parent` the subagent request names, the row is never visited — and the same mismatch would explain why the stick that turn's completion wrote wasn't found either. Your subagent #2 finding both lookups at +33 s says the spawning turn's ids do match, so a mismatch would have to sit between the two lead turns, not between lead and gate.

What would tell them apart: the +12.5 s row's Session/NativeSession value next to the parent id the subagent request carried, and whether other calls were completing on that instance in the +12.5 s→+21.0 s window.

**Fix directions — the maintainer's call, each with a cost**, since the gate is deliberately fail-closed (a sealed task handed to a provider that didn't answer the lead is the `invalid_encrypted_content` failure 3b961f294 fixed):

- The one you suggested — count the in-flight answerer. Routing already remembers where a conversation's un-answered request went (`sticks.opening`, "who a conversation that nobody has answered yet was sent to, while its first request is out") — but only on multi-candidate routes, and it is deleted the moment the answer lands. A gate that also consulted the in-flight record for the parent would cover exactly your window.
- Force a settled read for this one lookup (bypass the settle stamp), at the cost of a re-hash on every sealed-task miss.
- Binding at dispatch instead of completion would stick the conversation to a provider that may then fail the turn — that shape is probably worse than the hole.

Not verified: your relay's real traffic — this is the code at `f6c882ad7` plus your timeline; I didn't replay a Sub2API relay.

## Summary

The branch of #141/#613 that no fix reached is the relay. On a vendor serving the Responses API natively, Codex's request is relayed as it came (`Server.passthrough`, internal/gateway/gateway.go:4179) — and the vendor's reply went back as it came too. A vendor that answers `collaboration.spawn_agent` with its plain-text arguments but no `encrypted_function_args` field (exactly what the issue's probe recorded: namespace kept, arguments kept, no list) handed Codex a call Codex cannot read as a plain-text task: `ToolCall::direct_source` (codex-rs tools/router.rs, rust-v0.163.0) picks `DirectPlaintextMessage` only when `encrypted_function_args` is present and empty. So Codex took the task for sealed, wrapped the readable message in an `encrypted_content` of its own under the NEW_TASK header, and the subagent — handed ciphertext it cannot open, which is really plain text — asked what the task was and did nothing. That is the issue's item 3-5.

The translated path has said "not sealed" since #613: `callTo` gives every namespaced call `encrypted_function_args: []` (internal/gateway/responses.go:1711, "Nothing magpie serves seals arguments"). The Grok and Zed relays have had it through `nsTidy` since #404 (internal/gateway/grok_namespace.go). The one place neither reached is the relay to any other vendor: `namespacedIn` was read only for Grok and Zed (internal/gateway/gateway.go:4385 at base), so no relayed reply ever carried the word.

## Cause

The relay's response side passes a vendor's reply through a row of small tidies, and the only one that knows Codex's namespaces was gated to two plugins. A vendor asked as Codex sends it keeps the namespace in its tools and says it back on the call; what is missing from its reply is not the name, it is the empty list — the one bit Codex reads to tell a plain-text task from a sealed one. Nothing magpie serves seals arguments on this path either: the marks in spawn_agent's schema go upstream only as schema, and the issue's probe confirms the vendor answers 200 with plain arguments and no list.

## Fix

The namespaced tools a Responses request offers are now read on every relay, not only Grok's and Zed's (internal/gateway/gateway.go, the `named` computation in `passthrough`), and `nsTidy.call` (internal/gateway/grok_namespace.go) now also handles a call whose namespace the upstream named itself: when (namespace, name) matches a tool the request offered and the call carries no `encrypted_function_args`, the empty list is added — the same shape `callTo` gives the translated path. A call that does carry a seal — OpenAI's own, or any upstream that answers the mark — goes back with that seal untouched, and a call to a tool outside every namespace says nothing about seals either way (both locked by `TestNativeRelayLeavesOtherCallsBe`). The loop closes on the way back: the field Codex replays of it in a later turn's history is still what `forVendor` leaves out of what a non-OpenAI vendor is asked (`openaiOnly`, internal/gateway/codex_backend.go:2422), so the vendor never sees it.

## Verification

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `TestNativeRelayNamespacedCallSaysUnsealed` (stub vendor, stream and whole; asserts the relay, not a translation, and the empty list on every function_call Codex reads) | red on base, green with the fix |
| ablation: fix removed (`git checkout` of the two source files) | red, same assertion, `native_relay_collab_test.go:122`; fix restored, green |
| mutation: the list filled (`[]any{""}`) | red — a non-empty list is not "unsealed"; restored, green |
| `TestNativeRelayLeavesOtherCallsBe` (sealed call, plain call) | green: the seal survives, the plain call stays bare |
| `go test ./internal/gateway -count=1` (full package) | ok 322.6s |
| the new tests + the #404/#613 namespace tests, `-race` | ok |
| `gofmt -l`, `go vet ./internal/gateway` | clean |
| `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -tags nogui` darwin/arm64, linux/amd64, windows/amd64 | ok |

## Not verified

Not tried against the reporter's vendor or a real Codex Desktop; the stub's reply is the shape their probe recorded. The issue's second wish — a plaintext `agent_message` input item an upstream doesn't know turned into task text (their hand-built probe's 400 `unknown type: agent_message`) — is not addressed here: the real V2 rollout failed at the classification, before any `agent_message` went upstream, and reshaping every relayed conversation that carries one is a separate decision (the Grok relay does it in `grokAgentMessage`; a native relay doing it for every vendor is a bigger change than this branch needs).

---

**Source**: reported in #3183 (john-zeng-233, with V2 rollout records).

**Red without the fix** (base `f5b01574`):

```
--- FAIL: TestNativeRelayNamespacedCallSaysUnsealed (0.11s)
    native_relay_collab_test.go:122: stream true: Codex was given map[arguments: call_id:c9 id:fc_1 name:spawn_agent namespace:collaboration type:function_call]
FAIL
FAIL	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gateway	1.009s
```

(the call Codex was given carries no `encrypted_function_args` — the issue's item 3.)

**Siblings**: the field has three handling points, all now saying the same thing. The translated path adds the empty list in `callTo` (internal/gateway/responses.go:1711, #613); the request side strips what Codex replays of it before a non-OpenAI vendor is asked (`forVendor`/`openaiOnly`, internal/gateway/codex_backend.go:2422); the relay now adds it in `nsTidy.call` for a call named with its namespace (and, as since #404, renames a flat `collaboration__spawn_agent` back for the plugins that were offered it flat). No other spot in the tree reads or writes the field. The V1 spawn path, the spawn_agent models list and the session viewers do not touch it.

**When an upstream seals for real**: a reply whose namespaced call carries `encrypted_function_args` — OpenAI's own relays, or a vendor that honours the schema mark — passes with its seal exactly as it came; the fix adds nothing beside an absent list, and Codex's own handling of a seal it cannot open is unchanged.

```patch
+		}
+		// relayed, not translated: the namespace went up as Codex sent it
+		mu.Lock()
+		if len(sent) != 1 {
+			t.Fatalf("stream %v: the vendor was asked %d times", stream, len(sent))
+		}
+		q := sent[0]
+		mu.Unlock()
+		tools, _ := q["tools"].([]any)
+		if len(tools) != 2 {
+			t.Fatalf("stream %v: the vendor was offered %v", stream, q["tools"])
+		}
+		if tm, _ := tools[1].(map[string]any); tm["type"] != "namespace" || tm["name"] != "collaboration" {
+			t.Fatalf("stream %v: the request was translated, its tools went as %v", stream, q["tools"])
+		}
+
+		// every function_call Codex reads says its arguments are plain text
+		var items []map[string]any
+		if stream {
+			for _, line := range strings.Split(rec.Body.String(), "\n") {
+				data, ok := strings.CutPrefix(line, "data: ")
+				if !ok {
+					continue
+				}
+				var ev struct {
+					Item     map[string]any `json:"item"`
+					Response struct {
+						Output []map[string]any `json:"output"`
+					} `json:"response"`
+				}
+				if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(data), &ev); err != nil {
+					t.Fatalf("%v: %s", err, data)
+				}
+				if ev.Item != nil {
+					items = append(items, ev.Item)
+				}
+				items = append(items, ev.Response.Output...)
+			}
+		} else {
+			var res struct {
+				Output []map[string]any `json:"output"`
+			}
+			if err := json.Unmarshal(rec.Body.Bytes(), &res); err != nil {
+				t.Fatalf("%v: %s", err, rec.Body)
+			}
+			items = res.Output
+		}
+		if len(items) == 0 || stream && len(items) != 3 {
+			t.Fatalf("stream %v: %s", stream, rec.Body)
+		}
+		for _, it := range items {
+			sealed, ok := it["encrypted_function_args"].([]any)
+			if it["name"] != "spawn_agent" || it["namespace"] != "collaboration" || !ok || len(sealed) != 0 {
+				t.Fatalf("stream %v: Codex was given %v", stream, it)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+// The seal a reply carries is the seal the client reads: an upstream that
+// answered a namespaced call with its arguments sealed hands that seal on
+// untouched, and a call to a tool outside every namespace says nothing
+// about seals either way (#3183).
+func TestNativeRelayLeavesOtherCallsBe(t *testing.T) {
+	fresh(t)
+	sealed := `{"type":"function_call","id":"fc_1","call_id":"c9","name":"spawn_agent","namespace":"collaboration","arguments":"","encrypted_function_args":[{"content":"gAAAAAsealed"}],"status":"completed"}`
+	plain := `{"type":"function_call","id":"fc_2","call_id":"c8","name":"exec_command","arguments":"{}","status":"completed"}`
+	up := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+		io.ReadAll(r.Body)
+		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
+		io.WriteString(w, `{"id":"r1","object":"response","status":"completed","output":[`+sealed+`,`+plain+`],"usage":{"input_tokens":5,"output_tokens":3}}`)
+	}))
+	defer up.Close()
+	if err := provider.Save(provider.Provider{ID: "ucloud", Name: "UCloud", Key: "k", Models: []string{"m"}, Responses: up.URL + "/v1"}); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	s := New()
+	body := `{"model":"ucloud/m","stream":false,` + codexCollabTools + `,"input":[{"type":"message","role":"user","content":"go"}]}`
+	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
+	s.Handler().ServeHTTP(rec, httptest.NewRequest("POST", "/v1/responses", strings.NewReader(body)))
+	if rec.Code != 200 {
+		t.Fatalf("%d %s", rec.Code, rec.Body)
+	}
+	var res struct {
+		Output []map[string]any `json:"output"`
+	}
+	if err := json.Unmarshal(rec.Body.Bytes(), &res); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if len(res.Output) != 2 {
+		t.Fatalf("%s", rec.Body.String())
+	}
+	if got, ok := res.Output[0]["encrypted_function_args"].([]any); !ok || len(got) != 1 {
+		t.Fatalf("the seal was lost: %v", res.Output[0])
+	}
+	if _, ok := res.Output[1]["encrypted_function_args"]; ok {
+		t.Fatalf("a plain call was given a seal: %v", res.Output[1])
+	}
+}
-- 
2.50.1 (Apple Git-155)

```

Implemented both parts on my fork: [b1ae66c7](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/b1ae66c779355c897eed2337f83666447ae8db2a). The response-side fix and its original tests are adapted from ggbdpq's patch, with attribution retained.

For third-party Responses relays, an offered native namespaced function call now receives `encrypted_function_args: []` when that field is absent. Existing sealed arguments and unrelated calls remain unchanged. Official OpenAI/ChatGPT routes are excluded. This matches the direct collaboration call contract in Codex `rust-v0.163.0-alpha.10`.

On requests to third-party relays, plaintext `agent_message` input is converted using the existing provider helper into a normal user message, preserving its sender/recipient header and text/image content. Internal metadata is removed. Unsupported or sealed content remains opaque, and official OpenAI/ChatGPT requests keep their existing path. Copilot retains its native `agent_message` support, including its web search tools ([follow-up](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/eae195b)).

Regression tests cover streaming and whole replies, sealed/unrelated calls, plaintext text plus image input, metadata removal, and the official OpenAI route. Restoring the previous implementation makes both the response-marker and request-conversion tests fail. Focused gateway/provider tests, including the existing Copilot subagent and relay cases, passed with the race detector, three runs.

Validation uses local HTTP fixtures and a stub transport; I have not run a real Codex V2 session against a third-party vendor.

Combined branch: [fix/issue-batch-20261023-g](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/issue-batch-20261023-g), tested at `4b137b7073fe9fac3edea323ca221f7b26d5653f`. Go 1.26.8: native/Linux nogui/Windows vet and builds all passed, plus the full `go test -tags nogui ./... -count=1 -timeout=45m` suite in a temporary HOME. No upstream PR opened.

Verified the fork commit on top of `63be4771` (Windows, Go 1.26.8): cherry-picked b1ae66c7, ran the collaboration family in both packages, and reproduced both halves' regressions with the product files reverted.

**What was verified**

- Response side adapted from my `9fff5bab` faithfully: the `nsTidy.call` change and the first 167 lines of `native_relay_collab_test.go` are verbatim identical to my patch (the file is created fresh in this commit — its parent does not contain mine — so the commit is self-contained).
- The "other half" is the request side my patch explicitly deferred, and it has its own independent test: `forVendor` turns a plaintext `agent_message` into a user message via `provider.PlainAgentMessage` (the existing Grok converter, exported), `openaiOnly` gains an `"agent_message"` probe, and `TestNativeRelayPlainAgentMessage` locks the conversion, the preserved sender/recipient/image, metadata removal, and the sealed/unsupported negatives.
- One deliberate divergence from my patch, locked by `TestNativeRelayOpenAICallUnchanged`: the relay gate excludes a Codex account and `openai.com` hosts, so native OpenAI/ChatGPT replies are never touched, where mine read namespaces on every relay and relied on "a seal present stays untouched". More conservative on the official routes; behavior on third-party vendors is the same.
- Attribution in the commit is present and exact: `Co-authored-by: ggbdpq <ggbdpq@gmail.com>`, with "Adapt ggbdpq/magpie 9fff5bab..." in the message. Author: vincent.

**Red without the fix** (gateway.go, grok_namespace.go, codex_backend.go, provider/grok.go reverted to base, tests kept):

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Four new tests, product files at base | `go test -tags nogui -run '^(TestNativeRelayNamespacedCallSaysUnsealed\|TestNativeRelayLeavesOtherCallsBe\|TestNativeRelayPlainAgentMessage\|TestNativeRelayOpenAICallUnchanged)$' ./internal/gateway/` | 2 FAIL |
| Same, fix restored | same command | ok 1.983s |
| Relay/grok family with the fix | 8 gateway + 7 provider tests | ok |
| New tests under the detector | `-race -count=3` | ok 6.712s |

The two reds are the two halves:

```
--- FAIL: TestNativeRelayNamespacedCallSaysUnsealed (0.57s)
    native_relay_collab_test.go:122: stream true: Codex was given map[arguments: call_id:c9 id:fc_1 name:spawn_agent namespace:collaboration type:function_call]
--- FAIL: TestNativeRelayPlainAgentMessage (0.21s)
    native_relay_collab_test.go:191: task wasn't converted: {"input":[{"author":"/root",...,"type":"agent_message"}],...}
```

The first is my original patch's own red assertion, same line — the call reaches Codex with no `encrypted_function_args`. The second is the request half. The other two tests pass on the old code too (protective, not red evidence).

**Drift and landing**: the fork's parent is 467 commits ahead of `63be4771`; three conflicts on this base, all from later-upstream structure this base lacks — `forVendorChanges` does not exist here (its role is covered by the `openaiOnly` probe plus `forVendor` itself, both of which carry the change), `provider/grok.go` here has no `grokPluginBody`/`grokShaped` split (only the rename and comment are taken), and the docs paragraph arrives mixed with a `#3205` Kimi paragraph this base predates (dropped). Lands with those adjustments; the `nsTidy.call` hunk, the test file, and the `forVendor` conversion apply as written. On today's main (`e00fbdbb`, checked 2026-10-23) the commit's whole diff applies clean (`apply --3way --check`); neither half has landed upstream.

**Gaps**: unchanged from the report — no real Codex V2 session against a third-party vendor on either side; the stub's reply is the shape the reporter's probe recorded. The `gateway-routing.md` paragraph as written references the Kimi section that follows it on newer bases; on this base it stands alone. `gofmt -l` on the five files and `go vet -tags nogui` of both packages are clean. `rg encrypted_function_args` over non-test code shows exactly the four handling points the report names — no fifth reader.

Thanks — picking up the request side closes the loop my patch left open, and the OpenAI-route exclusion with its own test is a fair answer to a question my patch dodged.

issue.title: [Bug] Codex subagent tasks are ignored when sent as agent_message through Magpie 0.1.1333

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### Summary

Codex subagents start successfully and return responses, but do not act on their assigned tasks when using Magpie 0.1.1333 with `deepseek/deepseek-flash`.

The task is present in the Codex subagent's local session log as a Responses input item with `type: "agent_message"`. However, the model responds as though no task was provided.

Direct requests to Magpie reproduce the same behavior without involving Codex: an ordinary user `message` works, while an `agent_message` containing the same task does not. Both requests return HTTP 200.

### Environment

- **Magpie version:** `0.1.1333`
- **Codex CLI/core version:** `0.163.0-alpha.10.2`
- **Client:** Codex Desktop on Windows
- **Requested subagent model:** `deepseek/deepseek-flash`
- **Model reported in direct API responses:** `deepseek-flash`
- **Subagent reasoning effort recorded by Codex:** `high`
- **Configured Codex base URL:** `http://127.0.0.1:3425/backend-api/codex`
- **Endpoint used for reproduction:** `POST /backend-api/codex/responses`

Project names in the examples below have been anonymized as `example-project`.

### Expected Behavior

A task carried in a Codex `agent_message` input item should reach the downstream model, allowing the subagent to execute the task.

If this input type is unsupported, an explicit error would be preferable to returning HTTP 200 while the model appears not to receive the task.

### Actual Behavior

The subagent starts and replies, but asks for a task instead of executing the task already provided.

Examples of actual replies, translated from Chinese and anonymized:

> Please tell me what task you want to complete in example-project.

> I am ready to begin working in the current workspace. Please provide the specific requirements.

The subagent makes **zero tool calls**.

This occurred with:
- A minimal read-only command execution task.
- A follow-up task sent to the same subagent.
- A newly created subagent receiving another minimal task.
- A larger, detailed, read-only repository analysis task.

Increasing task size or sending a follow-up did not resolve the issue.

### Steps to Reproduce in Codex

1. Run Codex Desktop through Magpie 0.1.1333.
2. Configure or explicitly select `deepseek/deepseek-flash` as the subagent model.
3. Create a subagent with a concrete task, such as:
   - Execute a read-only PowerShell command.
   - Calculate `19 * 29`.
   - Return `MINIMAL_RETEST_OK|551`.
4. Observe that the subagent asks for a task rather than executing it.
5. Inspect the subagent session log:
   - `turn_context.model` is `deepseek/deepseek-flash`.
   - The assigned task is present as a `response_item` with `type: "agent_message"`.
   - No tool calls occur.

### Minimal API Reproduction — No Codex Required

The following two requests use the same model, the same initial user message, and the same task text. The task item's message type and associated envelope fields are the only intentional differences.

#### A. Ordinary user message — succeeds

```json
{
  "model": "deepseek/deepseek-flash",
  "stream": false,
  "max_output_tokens": 256,
  "input": [
    {
      "type": "message",
      "role": "user",
      "content": [
        {
          "type": "input_text",
          "text": "You are ready to receive a task."
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "type": "message",
      "role": "user",
      "content": [
        {
          "type": "input_text",
          "text": "Message Type: NEW_TASK\nTask name: /root/format_probe\nSender: /root\nPayload:\nReply with exactly FORMAT_PROBE_OK_842. Do not ask for a task."
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Send to:

```text
POST http://127.0.0.1:3425/backend-api/codex/responses
Content-Type: application/json
```

Observed result:

```text
HTTP 200
Response model: deepseek-flash
Assistant output: FORMAT_PROBE_OK_842
```

#### B. Codex-style agent_message — fails to follow the task

```json
{
  "model": "deepseek/deepseek-flash",
  "stream": false,
  "max_output_tokens": 256,
  "input": [
    {
      "type": "message",
      "role": "user",
      "content": [
        {
          "type": "input_text",
          "text": "You are ready to receive a task."
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "type": "agent_message",
      "id": "amsg_format_probe_842",
      "author": "/root",
      "recipient": "/root/format_probe",
      "content": [
        {
          "type": "input_text",
          "text": "Message Type: NEW_TASK\nTask name: /root/format_probe\nSender: /root\nPayload:\nReply with exactly FORMAT_PROBE_OK_842. Do not ask for a task."
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Send to the same endpoint.

Observed result:

```text
HTTP 200
Response model: deepseek-flash
Assistant output: Ready. Please provide the task.
```

### Reproduction Results

Two pairs of direct API requests were tested, with consistent results:

| Test | Task input type | HTTP status | Result |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Pair 1, control | `message` / `user` | 200 | Returned the requested marker |
| Pair 1, agent task | `agent_message` | 200 | Asked for a task |
| Pair 2, matched control | `message` / `user` | 200 | Returned `FORMAT_PROBE_OK_842` |
| Pair 2, agent task | `agent_message` | 200 | Replied: `Ready. Please provide the task.` |

Pair 2 used the matched payloads shown above.

### Relevant Codex Log Evidence

The actual repository-analysis task was recorded in the subagent session log in this structure. Identifiers and content below are shortened or anonymized:

```json
{
  "type": "response_item",
  "payload": {
    "type": "agent_message",
    "id": "amsg_...",
    "author": "/root",
    "recipient": "/root/project_analysis_test",
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "input_text",
        "text": "Message Type: NEW_TASK\nTask name: /root/project_analysis_test\nSender: /root\nPayload:\n[Complete repository analysis instructions for example-project]\nPROJECT_ANALYSIS_TEST_DONE"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Checks confirmed that:
- The full task text was present.
- The completion marker was present.
- The Chinese task text was intact, with no Unicode replacement characters.
- The actual subagent model matched the requested model.
- Magpie recorded HTTP 200 for the corresponding request.

**Important diagnostic detail:** filtering Codex logs only for `payload.type == "message"` misses these task items. They are stored as `payload.type == "agent_message"`.

### Suspected Cause / Investigation Pointers

This appears to be a compatibility issue in the handling or downstream conversion of Codex `agent_message` input items.

Please check whether:
1. The Responses input parser recognizes `agent_message`.
2. Its `content` is retained during request normalization.
3. The downstream provider adapter converts it into a message format supported by the target model.
4. Unrecognized input item types are silently skipped.

This is a hypothesis, not a confirmed internal root cause. I have not captured the raw request body sent from Magpie to DeepSeek, so I cannot yet determine whether the content is dropped inside Magpie or passed onward in a format the downstream API does not handle.

However, reproducing the issue through direct HTTP requests removes Codex task creation and scheduling from the minimal reproduction.

### Impact

Codex subagent delegation is effectively unusable in this tested configuration: subagents launch successfully but do not act on their assigned task instructions.

Because the requests return HTTP 200 and the subagents produce plausible readiness replies, the failure can be mistaken for a model instruction-following issue rather than a message-format compatibility problem.

### Scope and Workaround

- Confirmed with `deepseek/deepseek-flash` through Magpie 0.1.1333.
- Other downstream models/providers have not been tested in this investigation.
- Ordinary user messages work in direct API tests.
- The available Codex subagent tools do not expose an option to change the underlying task item from `agent_message` to an ordinary user `message`, so the direct API workaround does not fix normal subagent delegation.

issue.title: [兼容] Codex V2 自定义 agents namespace：已有明文标记仍丢任务，安全适配实测通过（v0.1.2119）

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## 摘要

关联 #141、#3183、#3374、#4108，但本例有一个重要差异：**父调用已经明确携带 `encrypted_function_args: []`，Codex 仍把明文任务写进子会话的 `encrypted_content`。** 触发条件是自定义协作命名空间 `agents`，而该 Codex 版本的明文判定只认 `collaboration`。

这部分是 Codex 上游的分类缺陷，不应全部归责于 Magpie。本 issue 希望跟踪：Magpie 对这一组合的兼容/诊断边界，以及第三方 Responses 中继能否内置安全的明文任务适配，避免用户依赖外置代理。

## 实测环境

- Windows x64，Codex Desktop 内置 `codex-cli 0.166.0-alpha.5.1`，不是并存的 npm CLI。
- Magpie `v0.1.2119`，构建提交 `ffa07395eb274cbe6cea299d825bf4f5c58db6e2`。
- 链路：Codex → 本机 Magpie `:3425/v1` → 自定义 AxonHub Responses 中转 → 模型。
- 主模型：`axonhub/gpt-6.1-sol`；原生 `default` 子代理：`gpt-6-luna`。最初故障样本的主模型也有 `axonhub/gpt-6-luna`。
- `wire_api="responses"`，V2 开启，`tool_namespace="agents"`；`fork_turns="none"`。
- 以下实测为 Desktop 内置后端的真实 CLI 验收。Desktop 配置已应用，但**不宣称已完成 Desktop UI 重启后的验收**。

## 原始记录中实际发生的事

父会话完成的工具调用（任务内容替换为无关测试口令）：

```json
{
  "type": "function_call",
  "name": "spawn_agent",
  "namespace": "agents",
  "encrypted_function_args": [],
  "arguments": "{\"task_name\":\"alpha\",\"fork_turns\":\"none\",\"message\":\"Reply with exactly TEST_TOKEN\"}"
}
```

子会话收到：

```json
{
  "type": "agent_message",
  "author": "/root",
  "recipient": "/root/alpha",
  "content": [
    {"type":"input_text","text":"Message Type: NEW_TASK\nTask name: /root/alpha\nSender: /root\nPayload:\n"},
    {"type":"encrypted_content","encrypted_content":"Reply with exactly TEST_TOKEN"}
  ]
}
```

两个原始故障样本中，该块分别为 295 / 339 个字符；脚本逐字比对确认其与父级明文 `message` 完全相同，不是真实加密后的内容。子代理均正常启动并返回，但回复“Payload 为空 / 未收到具体检索任务”。send/receive 的 communication ID 对应，返回父级的 FINAL_ANSWER 明文可正常收到。

### 对应的上游判定

精确版本源码：[ToolCall::direct_source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.166.0-alpha.5.1/codex-rs/core/src/tools/router.rs#L56)。其条件含：

```rust
self.tool_name.namespace.as_deref() == Some("collaboration")
// ... spawn_agent / send_message / followup_task ...
&& self.encrypted_function_args.as_ref().is_some_and(Vec::is_empty)
```

因此 `agents` + 明确空加密字段名单仍走 `Direct`；随后 [agent_message_from_tool](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.166.0-alpha.5.1/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_v2.rs#L54) 把它归为 `AgentMessage::Encrypted`。

所以**只补空加密字段名单并不能修复这个变体**；本例也不是请求 Magpie 解密真正的 OpenAI 密文。

## 已验证的本地兼容办法

实现一个仅绑定 loopback 的轻量 HTTP/SSE 适配层，置于 Codex 与 Magpie 之间，不改模型名、工具 schema、认证或 Magpie 路由：

1. 只观察请求实际提供的原生协作工具；只有完成的工具调用明确带 `encrypted_function_args: []` 时，登记其 message 的 SHA256，内存有限容量和过期时间，不落盘任务正文。
2. 对明文 `agent_message`，完整转换为普通 `message` / `role=user`，保留发送者、接收者、任务文本；不提升为 system/developer 权限。
3. 对错误标记的 `encrypted_content`，只有精确匹配此前登记的明文摘要才恢复；未知、真正密文或不支持的内容明确 422 拒绝。不是根据 `gAAAA` 前缀等外观猜测密文。
4. SSE 响应字节原样转发，不修改模型路由。

### 真实单轮 Codex CLI 结果

在一个 `codex exec` 用户 turn 内，要求模型实际创建 alpha/beta 两个原生 V2 子代理、不继承父历史，分别返回不同随机口令；向原 alpha 追加一次任务；再执行一个普通 shell 控制命令。

- 两个子代理初始回复精确匹配各自口令。
- 原 alpha 的 followup 精确匹配新口令。
- shell 真实执行事件与输出匹配。
- 模型最终 JSON 的 `errors=[]`。
- 独立读取原生子线程完成记录核对，而不是只相信父模型自报成功。
- 用全局 provider 地址、不传一次性 endpoint 覆盖的复测用时约 41 秒，CLI 退出 0，全部验收检查通过。
- 适配层恢复 4 个任务块（包括历史重放），对应 3 个不同 payload；拒绝与上游错误均为 0；模型/provider 响应头仍为原 axonhub 路由。
- 另有 15 项单元/HTTP 集成测试，覆盖精确明文登记、拒绝未知密文、UTF-8 SSE 分片、认证/会话头转发、断流和普通消息不变，全部通过。

这里不上传完整会话、全量配置、认证文件或真实 HTTP 请求头。

## 范围限制，避免误判

- 历史 AxonHub 请求正文未留存，也未取得 Magpie 与 AxonHub 间的入口/出口双点抓包，因此**不能断言实际第一个丢弃点一定在 Magpie 内部**。
- 本机 AxonHub 源码转换函数已用 Go overlay 离线复现：未知 `agent_message` 被跳过；仅改外层类型仍丢内部 `encrypted_content`；完整转换为普通用户文本可保留。这个事实不能等同于已验证运行镜像每个字节与工作树一致。
- 明文误标为密文是同版本 Codex 源码和父子会话等值比对已证实的；下游需要 provider-aware 消息适配，与 #4108 的兼容范围相邻。
- 本轮真实测试覆盖 spawn/followup，**没有单独实测运行中 send_message**。
- 外置适配层不提供真实密文解密，重启/过期后无法安全恢复旧会话的未知任务。

## 期望与建议

1. 请确认 native Responses relay 对此类明文 `agent_message` 的覆盖范围；对真正支持加密代理消息的 OpenAI 等后端保留原生路径，不全局拍平成 user。
2. 对第三方不支持的代理输入，优先安全适配或明确报错，不要出现“HTTP 200 + 子代理没任务”的假成功。
3. 针对 `agents` + 明确空加密字段名单，能否提示 Codex 上游 namespace 条件限制、跟踪其修复，或提供有边界的兼容方式？不建议简单改回 `collaboration`，因为此前还存在 reserved namespace/schema 兼容问题。
4. 外置办法需要把 Codex 地址改到另一端口，而 Magpie 后续重生成 Codex 配置**可能**恢复 `:3425`、绕过适配层。这个覆盖尚未在本次实测触发，列为维护风险而非已证实的新回归。若原生修复暂不可行，希望提供受支持的外置适配/连接地址选项，避免双方抢写配置；内置适配会更省心。

### 推荐回归测试

- 分别覆盖默认与自定义 namespace、空名单/缺失名单/真正加密参数、JSON 与 SSE 响应。
- 分别覆盖第三方 Responses relay 与原生支持 agent_message 的后端。
- 原生 Codex V2 spawn + followup 使用不同随机口令，并核对实际子线程结果，不能只看 200 或退出码。
- 用户修改 Magpie 的 Codex 设置后，仍走受支持的修复链路或有明确提示。

如果本问题适合并入既有 issue，请关联/合并；关键补充是 **v0.1.2119 + Codex 0.166 的自定义 namespace 明文误分类，以及已通过真实 CLI 的精确明文适配证据**。

issue.title: DeepSeek subagents in Codex get no task: relayed Responses requests keep agent_message (fix in fork)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Problem

A Codex subagent on DeepSeek receives no task. It sees only the AGENTS.md instructions and replies with a request for a task, for example "请说明本次任务". DeepSeek returns no error.

Tested on Magpie v0.1.1734 with the built-in DeepSeek provider (`deepseek/deepseek-flash`). The provider has both `chat` and `responses` URLs at `https://api.deepseek.com/v1`. The Codex desktop app uses MultiAgentV2.

## Trigger

In MultiAgentV2, Codex gives a subagent its task, and gives the lead the subagent's reply, as an `agent_message` input item:

```json
{"type":"agent_message","author":"/root","recipient":"/root/probe","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"Message Type: NEW_TASK\nPayload:\n..."}]}
```

Magpie relays Codex's `/v1/responses` request to DeepSeek's Responses API. `passthrough` applies `forVendor`, but no step changes `agent_message` for this upstream. DeepSeek drops the unknown item and answers the rest of the input. Magpie already sends this item as a user turn when it translates a request (`readResponses`), and when it sends a request to Grok (`grokAgentMessage`, plugins#61). It does not do this for other relayed Responses APIs.

The `codex exec` CLI path did not reproduce the problem because it sends the task as a plain user message.

## Live comparison

A minimal `/v1/responses` request to the gateway has an AGENTS.md user message, followed by an `agent_message` that asks for the passphrase `蓝鲸-4471`:

| Gateway | DeepSeek answer |
| --- | --- |
| v0.1.1734 | Acknowledges the AGENTS.md text and asks what to do |
| With the fix below | `蓝鲸-4471` |

In a full Codex app-server run with the fix, a DeepSeek lead spawned a DeepSeek subagent. The subagent returned the passphrase that appeared only in its task.

## Fix

- [Commit 8696b50](https://github.com/hqhq1025/magpie/commit/8696b500ea4f1c425c914e2ec4eec1a76cd5eb96) on top of `b692de9`
- [Branch diff](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/main...hqhq1025:magpie:fix/third-party-responses-agent-message)

For a relayed Responses request, Magpie now sends each plain `agent_message` as a user message. It names the sender and recipient first, as `grokAgentMessage` does. This applies only to upstreams other than OpenAI's API, the ChatGPT backend, Azure OpenAI, Copilot, and another Magpie. Those upstreams receive the item unchanged: Azure requires the item's `author`, and `TestCopilotUltraSubagentWithWebSearch` (#656) already requires Copilot to receive it as Codex sent it. A sealed `agent_message` (`encrypted_content`) is left unchanged on every upstream.


## Validation

- `TestThirdPartyResponsesGetAgentMessageAsUser` relays `agentMessageTurn` to a Responses provider. Without the fix it fails with `the upstream was sent an agent_message`. With Azure removed from the kept list, its Azure case fails with `Azure was not sent the agent_message as it came`. Both pass with the fix.
- `gofmt -l` prints nothing. `go vet ./...`, `GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui ./...`, `GOOS=windows go vet ./...`, and the three builds pass.
- Under a temporary HOME with pinned Go caches, `go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway` passes in 1168 s, and `./internal/agent` passes. In the full `./...` run on a laptop, `internal/agent` and `internal/gateway` hit the default 10-minute timeout; `TestStaleLatestIsNotUpToDate`, `TestRTKCheckLatestDoesNotWaitForThePackageManager` and `TestJustWrittenSkillIsReadAgain` failed on timing and pass when run alone. `TestIntentClassifierFails` failed once on its 800 ms classifier deadline under the same load and passes alone.
- Bun-based Grok plugin parity tests were skipped because the local Bun is 1.3.13.
- The fix is deployed on a Linux gateway. A Codex app-server DeepSeek lead and DeepSeek subagent completed the passphrase run above.

I could not open a PR because this repository restricts PR creation to collaborators. The fork commit is available for review or cherry-picking. The issue omits credentials and conversation content.

timeline.body:
我这边也遇到了和 @oevery 类似的情况，补充一组对照结果。

环境是 macOS，Magpie 0.1.3058，Codex 桌面内置后端 0.166.0-alpha.6，通过自定义 Responses 中转使用 gpt-6.1-sol。

用相同的业务输入分别直连上游和经过 Magpie，请求没有压缩项，也不执行模型生成的工具调用：

- 直连上游：`spawn_agent.message` 是 `gAAAA…` 格式的载荷，`encrypted_function_args` 字段缺失。
- 经过 Magpie：载荷仍是同类格式，但多了 `encrypted_function_args: []`。

实际 V2 子会话中也能看到，任务载荷被作为普通 `input_text` 交付，子代理回复无法读取任务。

对照 0.1.3058 的 `nsTidy.call`，这里会把缺失字段补成空数组。但对这种保留原生密封任务的中转，字段缺失似乎不能直接当作“参数是明文”。能否考虑让这类中转显式选择保留 Codex 原生加密标记的模式？仅凭 `gAAAA` 前缀判断也未必可靠。

补充一组与上面两条中转回归反馈一致的实测：**真实密文可以正常解密；只修正加密标记就恢复父子代理双向通信，恢复原网关行为后立即再次失败。** 另发现现有 fork 补丁没有覆盖本次 `arguments` 内嵌 JSON `message` 的数据形态。

**环境**

- Windows，Codex Desktop 内置后端 `0.167.0-alpha.3.2`，原生 `collaboration` / multi-agent V2。
- 实际采样和对照时 Magpie 为 `0.1.3335`，由应用启动日志确认。
- 自定义 API-key Responses 提供商，主、子代理均经同一提供商使用 `gpt-6-astra`；下文匿名记为 `relay/gpt-6-astra`。
- 2026-11-08，北京时间；测试发生在普通聊天中，不限于审查模式。

**1. 在 Magpie 改写前观察真实上游响应**

临时将该提供商的 Responses 地址指向仅监听 loopback 的转发器，再转发到原上游，沿用原网络代理和实际 Codex 请求。请求正文保持不变，没有伪造官方客户端标头。只保存必要协议元数据、长度和哈希，不记录凭据、完整对话或原始密文。

23:08 的同一次 `collaboration.followup_task`：

| 位置 | `encrypted_function_args` | 任务正文 / 接收方式 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 上游 → Magpie，改写前 | 字段缺失 | `arguments` 为 JSON 字符串，其中 `message` 是密文 |
| Codex 保存的工具调用 | `[]` | `message` 与上游完全相同 |
| 子代理收到的消息 | 已走明文投递 | `input_text` 含同一密文，子代理报告不可读 |

上游 SSE 的 `response.output_item.added`、`response.output_item.done`、`response.completed` 都缺少该字段，不是结束事件补回了标记。请求中的 `message.encrypted: true` 仍存在。完成事件、Codex 工具参数和接收端正文的 SHA-256 一致。

**2. 只改标记的真实对照实验**

23:32–23:33，继续使用同一个已有子代理。临时转发器只对这两个测试聊天的 `followup_task` / `send_message` 做诊断性修改：

- 对缺字段且 `arguments` 为空的初始 `output_item.added` 补 `encrypted_function_args: null`，避免 Magpie 补成空数组。
- 完成事件确认本次测试的 `message` 是密文形态后，给缺字段的调用补 `["message"]`；已有标记不覆盖。
- 不修改请求正文或消息密文；每次执行均核对上游、Codex 参数和接收端的正文哈希一致。这是受控诊断规则，不是建议直接上线的通用密文识别方案。

| 条件 | 观察到的实际结果 |
| --- | --- |
| 原网关行为 | 密文 + `[]` → `input_text`，消息不可读 |
| 仅修正标记 | Codex 保存 `["message"]`，接收端为 `encrypted_content`；追加任务、父到子的普通消息、子到父的普通消息均可读 |
| 23:34 恢复原网关 | 再次为 `[]` + `input_text`，同一子代理立即报告新任务不可读 |

第一次追加任务要求子代理通过 `send_message` 回传一个新口令，父代理能读懂，子代理最终答复也准确回传。第二次把另一个新口令仅放在父到子的普通消息里，再发不包含口令的追加任务要求读取它，子代理再次准确回传。没有用共享文件传任务或结果。共核对四次实际执行的修正调用，一次客户端取消后重试的生成尝试未算作成功执行。

转发器先通过 18 项隔离检查，涵盖透传/断流、JSON/SSE、会话范围、显式标记保留、当前实体网关保留修正标记，以及正常退出/超时/进程终止后的恢复。测试结束已恢复原 Responses 地址，提供商其他字段未变；没有替换正式网关二进制，也没有留下永久转发方案。

这组对照说明：本次密文的生成和解密链路可用，Magpie 的标记改写足以造成失败。历史上为何同一配置曾返回明文、后来返回密文仍未确定；不据此将变化归因于某次版本升级。本轮复用已有子代理，没有重新测试 `spawn_agent` 初始任务。

**3. `c20d3e202` 的覆盖缺口：密文在 JSON 的 `message` 里**

感谢提供 [fork 修复 c20d3e202](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/c20d3e202788edac7021d506a81207d04a315e08)。检查该提交发现，守卫对整个 `it["arguments"]` 字符串匹配：

```go
if args, _ := it["arguments"].(string); nativeSealedAgentPayload.MatchString(args) {
    return false
}
```

对应正则是 `^gAAAAA[A-Za-z0-9_-]+={0,2}$`，新增测试也把整个 `arguments` 直接设为 token。但本次真实结构是下面这样（值已替换，不是真实密文）：

```json
{
  "type": "function_call",
  "namespace": "collaboration",
  "name": "followup_task",
  "arguments": "{\"target\":\"/root/probe\",\"message\":\"gAAAAA...\"}"
}
```

对实际参数做只读核对：整个 `arguments` 不匹配该正则，解析后的 `message` 匹配。因此这个守卫不会保护本次形态；测试还需要覆盖嵌套字段，以及初始参数为空、参数完成、output-item 完成和整次 response 完成的 SSE 阶段。本次没有安装或运行该 fork，这一结论来自代码和实际报文结构核对。

查询时的主仓 `main` 及最新发布 [v0.1.3336 的 `nsTidy.call`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.3336/internal/gateway/grok_namespace.go#L186-L222) 仍在 namespace 匹配且缺字段时无条件补 `[]`。

希望修复能在保留真正明文提供商兼容行为的同时，保留支持原生密封消息的第三方 Responses 中转的加密语义，并覆盖上述 JSON 内 `message` 及流式阶段。这里补充的是实际边界采样和可逆干预证据，不主张只靠密文前缀就能完整判定所有提供商协议。

timeline.body:
@WilliamK7 谢谢这组边界采样及 A/B/A 实测。你指出的覆盖缺口成立：`c20d3e202` 只匹配整个 arguments；JSON 对象中的 `message` 不受它保护，初始空 arguments 也没有分类依据。此前我们把这个守卫描述成完整修复，范围说大了。

我在固定 main `b1e8eb15a668bbccfcd46977c75602ceaa4d66b3` 的真实 `/v1/responses` handler 上重现：嵌套 message、初始空参数、分段 delta、arguments.done、output_item.done 与 completed.response.output 都走过；缺字段的初始及完整调用均被补 `[]`，完整调用的参数保持原样。JSON 也重现。这里没有重跑你的真实 Codex 0.167 会话，也没有声称 `ed0ab567` 已验证。

目前不能把请求中的 `message.encrypted:true` 直接当作上游已经加密的证据：原始明文供应商也收到同一声明，却返回明文。前缀同样不能证明密文，也不能证明没有前缀的值一定是明文。缓冲到完整参数只解决初始空参数问题，补不出上游兑现了哪种契约。现有 `CodexAsSent` 只承诺请求按 Codex 原样发送，不承诺响应的加密语义。

需要先确定一个明确的兼容契约。我建议优先要求支持密封的中继输出参数级 `encrypted_function_args`：初始未知可为 null，完整密封调用声明 `["message"]`，明文调用明确 `[]`，Magpie 保留显式值。你的诊断规则所用“初始 null／完成 ["message"]”通过本地 handler 对照。若必须兼容上游始终不写标记的旧中继，则需维护者决定：是否把既有 Codex 原样模式扩展为双向契约，或增加独立的原生密封响应能力选择；默认明文供应商行为是否继续保留。这个决定会改变已有配置含义，不能由补丁用字符串前缀替代。

本轮没有上线自动密文判断或新设置。已归档可执行复现：缺标记密封验收在基线保持 RED；显式标记、明文、同字节字面量、无前缀不透明载荷、普通函数及官方 API 对照均有原始输出，相关 race、nogui vet/build 通过。待契约确定后再做最小适配，避免修一类中继时再次破坏另一类。

v0.1.3526 (a45dd9c65): a namespaced collaboration call a Responses relay returns without `encrypted_function_args` no longer always gets `[]`. When an argument holds a ChatGPT-sealed token (`gAAAAA…`, as CPA/Sub2API return `message`), it now gets that argument's name, e.g. `["message"]`, so Codex delivers it sealed instead of handing the ciphertext over as text. A plain relay still gets `[]`. Thanks to WilliamK7 for the real-traffic finding that `["message"]` restores two-way messages; please say whether lead and subagent can read each other again on this version.

@yetone Confirmed fixed on **Magpie 0.1.3531** in the previously affected Windows/Codex environment (Codex core `0.167.0-alpha.3.2`, the same custom Responses relay and `gpt-6-astra`).

I **disabled the local compatibility middleware before testing**, so the native fix was tested independently. At 14:31–14:32 UTC+8 on November 10:

- Lead → subagent `followup_task`: readable; a fresh nonce was echoed correctly.
- Lead → subagent `send_message`: a separate fresh nonce was read and echoed correctly.
- Subagent → lead `send_message`: both replies were readable.
- All **four executed calls** had `encrypted_function_args: ["message"]` in the Codex records. The corresponding receiver items were `encrypted_content`, with matching ciphertext hashes between sender arguments and received content.

No task/result files were used as a fallback. Provider and Codex configuration hashes were unchanged. The now-unneeded local middleware has been unregistered and removed.

A separate portable copy of the installed **0.1.3531 binary, with no middleware installed**, also passed **25 synthetic-upstream checks** covering JSON/SSE, the three collaboration tools, Responses Lite, plaintext behavior, preservation of explicit markers, and flushing the initial SSE item before completion.

Scope: the real test reused the existing subagent; it did not create a new one. `spawn_agent` was covered by the isolated gateway tests. For this previously failing relay/model, bidirectional communication is now working without the workaround. Thanks for the fix!

issue.title: [Bug] Responses HTTP 回程重建丢失 function_call 的 encrypted_function_args,密封的 collaboration 参数失去密文标记

repository.name: sub2api
repository.description: Sub2API 一站式开源中转服务，让 Claude、Openai 、Gemini、Grok订阅统一接入，支持拼车共享，更高效分摊成本，原生工具无缝使用。
